summary: Eight comment-endorsed discoveries: safer GitHub Actions, faster Rust builds, Socratic learning, research reading, thin-client hardware, drawing, CSV parsing, and speculative cosmology.
telegram_footer: 8 items surfaced | 30/30 past front-page stories processed | history + run artifact updated

items.name: actions-up

items.why_included: A direct endorsement identifies a practical tool for safer workflow updates.
items.evidence: A commenter calls themselves a big fan of actions-up in the workflow-locking discussion.

evidence_sources.author: transitivebs
evidence_sources.excerpt: big fan of actions-up for doing this:

items.name: mr boxington
items.source_story_title: Relax: JIT compiler for Rust to reduce build times
items.summary: Shared Cargo build cache that reuses compiler work across projects and worktrees.
items.why_included: Several weeks of positive first-hand use support this Rust-build alternative.
items.evidence: A commenter reports using mr boxington for several weeks and finding it a big help.

evidence_sources.author: jonstewart
evidence_sources.excerpt: I've been using "mr boxington" (mbx) the past several weeks and it's been a big help.

items.summary: Hardware reference for repurposing old thin clients into quiet homelab servers.

evidence_sources.author: NortySpock
evidence_sources.excerpt: Funny, I use that exact website to find passively cooled hardware to use as a server.

items.name: Socratic Tutor
items.summary: Jane Street's tutoring skill makes LLMs question your reasoning instead of spoon-feeding answers.
items.why_included: Two users independently praise the skill's effect on learning and independent thought.
items.evidence: Commenters prefer the skill's reduced handholding and report thinking more independently; they note that a simple prompt may reproduce the effect.

evidence_sources.author: arshxyz
evidence_sources.excerpt: I've used the same model for learning before and I definitely prefer using this skill because it stops the model from the usual handholding.

evidence_sources.author: Imanari
evidence_sources.excerpt: Socratic tutoring with LLMs works great for me and I have used this skill and it also works great (can you do the same with a simple prompt? probably) Using LLMs this way was really refreshing, I could really feel how I started to think on my own again.

items.name: alphaXiv
items.summary: AI-assisted research-paper reader, recommended for reading and understanding arXiv papers.
items.why_included: A reader explicitly recommends the service and explains their own use.
items.evidence: A commenter recommends alphaXiv to someone seeking help understanding papers and describes it as a better PDF reader for arXiv.

evidence_sources.author: lucrbvi
evidence_sources.excerpt: You should probably try [AlphaXiv](https://www.alphaxiv.org/), they are building what you want. I use it as a better PDF reader for arxiv paper but they are going all in on AI teaching/explaining things.
